topic: Itchy eyes: allergy basics — don't rub, cool compress, see a doctor

youtube.title: Itchy eyes? Don't rub! Do this instead 🙅 #Shorts
youtube.description:
Itchy eyes? Don't rub them. Here's what to do instead.
கண் அரிக்கிறதா? தேய்க்காதீர்கள்!

• Dust, pollen, pet hair or mould trigger eye allergy; the eye releases histamine, causing itching, redness and watering.
• DON'T rub: it releases more histamine and worsens the itch; hard rubbing over time can harm the cornea.
• DO use a cool compress: a clean, cool, damp cloth over closed eyes for a few minutes.
• DO wash hands and face after coming in, change pillow covers often, keep windows closed on dusty days.
• Allergy usually affects both eyes. One red, painful eye is a different problem.
• Don't use leftover or borrowed eye drops.
• See an eye specialist urgently for pain, blurred vision, light sensitivity or thick discharge.

gmb.text: Itchy eyes? Don't rub them. Dust, pollen or pet hair can trigger an allergy, and the eye releases histamine, which causes itching, redness and watering. Rubbing releases even more and makes the itch worse, and hard rubbing over time can harm the clear front of the eye. Instead, place a clean, cool, damp cloth over closed eyes for a few minutes, wash your hands and face after coming in from outside, and change pillow covers often. Don't use leftover or borrowed eye drops. See an eye specialist urgently if you have pain, blurred vision, light sensitivity or thick discharge. The eye test in our store is free.
